title: Toronto Police officer cleared in fatal shooting of man holding hostage
article: A Toronto cop has been cleared of any wrongdoing in the shooting death of a man who held a hostage at knifepoint in Scarborough last month.

Ontario Special Investigations Unit investigators determined the officer tried repeatedly to get Malcolm Jackman, 39, to drop his knife and she was ultimately forced to open fire to end the frightening situation, which has the hallmarks of a suicide by cop.

"Mr. Jackman represented an imminent threat of death or serious bodily harm to the citizen," SIU director Ian Scott said in a statement released Tuesday. "Accordingly, I am of the view that she had no reasonable choice but to discharge her firearm to stop this imminent threat to the person who the decedent had taken hostage."
The subject officer and her partner were dispatched June 8 with paramedics to deal with an emotionally disturbed person in an apartment at 140 Adanac Dr., near Eglinton Ave. E. and Markham Rd.
Upon arrival, a man approached and told them Jackman had attacked him with a knife at a bus stop.
The officers went into the building and found Jackman in a stairwell "talking to himself," Scott said.
The subject officer, whose name was not released, told the man to show his hands.
"He raised his hands over his head, displaying a knife in his right hand," Scott said. "Both officers drew their firearms and ordered Mr. Jackman to drop the knife.
"He shouted at the officers, asking them to shoot him as he paced to the left and the right brandishing the knife," Scott said.
The subject officer discharged her pepper spray but it had no effect. Jackman ran out of the building with the officers on his heels.
Outside, Jackman grabbed a citizen and held the knife near the hostage's throat, Scott said.
The officers repeatedly commanded Jackman at gunpoint to drop the knife.
"The subject officer observed Mr. Jackman moving the knife closer to his hostage's neck and discharged her firearm four times in his direction," Scott said, adding Jackman "fell to the ground."
Three of the bullets grazed Jackman in his leg, waist and arm. The fourth bullet to his abdomen killed him.
"In my view, the subject officer's use of lethal force was justified in these circumstances," Scott said.

Toronto Police spokesman Mark Pugash said the case highlights the dangers cops routinely face and the officer in this case "behaved to the highest standards of professionalism under very difficult circumstances."

"Mr. Scott acknowledges that the officer, under extreme pressure, used her training to try to resolve the situation with the least amount of force," Pugash said. "Unfortunately, it was necessary for her to use lethal force."
